study_identification_part.si_4_title: Mapping the Heterogeneous Phenotype of Schizophrenia and Bipolar Disorder Using Normative Models

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: All participants were recruited as part of the Thematically Organized Psychosis study (TOP).
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "All participants were recruited as part of the Thematically Organized Psychosis study..."

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Healthy individuals from TOP were used to estimate the normative model (10-fold CV for normative range, then trained on all for application). Patients from TOP were used to map deviations.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "we estimated the normative range for this model in healthy individuals under 10-fold cross-validation, then applied the model trained on all data to patients."

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: 256 healthy individuals were included. The model trained on all data was applied to patients.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "The study also included 256 healthy individuals... we estimated the normative range for this model in healthy individuals under 10-fold cross-validation, then applied the model trained on all data to patients."
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.location: Wolfers2018.pdf.md: Results / Paragraph 1; Methods / Normative Modeling
